clue.text: Complaint by player about new sponsor

indicators.note: about means going round, so the complaint's letters surround the abbreviation

parts.note: a beef is a grumble or complaint
an actor is a player on stage

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a theatre performer and a fresh backer for the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container; 'by' is only a link placing the player alongside. A beef is British slang for a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron who funds a cause or production is its backer, a synonym of sponsor.

clue.text: Black cat's springiness

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the ounce is the snow leopard, a big cat; the possessive 's is no letter

explanation.surface: A dark feline has a lively spring in its step.
explanation.walkthrough: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard.
explanation.definitionFit: Resilience or bounciness in a material or a step is its springiness.

clue.text: Portion of spinach omelette, part of a snack?

indicators.note: a portion is a piece of something, so the answer is a run of letters inside the next words

explanation.surface: A slice of spinach omelette is offered as a light bite.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'spinach omelette'; the question mark marks a nacho as one item of a plate of tortilla chips.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla chip topped with cheese is one piece of a Mexican snack dish.

clue.text: I'm found among fitters working on sound building for new purchaser

indicators.note: found among means placed in the middle of the rearranged letters
working suggests the letters of fitters are set in motion and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe

indicators.note: sound means the word is spoken, so a word said like the farm building is written

parts.note: a byre is a cowshed, a farm building

explanation.surface: Someone joins tradesmen working on a soundly built house for a novice homeowner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges the fitters' letters into FIRSTTE; 'sound' is the homophone signal, though the surface reads it as 'well built'. A byre is a cowshed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone purchasing their first home is a newcomer to the property market.

clue.text: Ditch girl during church social at last

indicators.note: during means the girl sits inside the other letters
at last points to the final letter of social

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman leaves a church social before it ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' takes L from 'social'. 'Ditch' looks like a verb (to dump) but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A channel is a dug watercourse, a trench or ditch.

clue.text: Order placed by university, getting in writer's book collection

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit

indicators.note: getting in means the university letter enters the pen's letters

parts.note: a nib is the point of a pen, a writer; with the possessive it gives an S

explanation.surface: A ceremonial honour is granted by a university to an author's collected works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placed by' only sets the pieces side by side. OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour; a writer here is a pen, whose point is a nib.
explanation.definitionFit: A single volume gathering several works by one author is a compendium.

clue.text: Companion has work cut out

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A friend finds the job has been removed.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the Companion of Honour, a British award; 'has' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe or remove something, as from a schedule, is to scrap it.

clue.text: Cake about a pound in Herts town

indicators.note: about means the first word's letters go round the second's

parts.note: to cake is to set hard, to harden
a pound for animals is an enclosure, a pen

explanation.surface: A sponge priced at a quid is on sale in a Hertfordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cake' looks like a noun but is the verb to set hard. Herts is Hertfordshire, a county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: This commuter place lies in Hertfordshire, abbreviated Herts.

clue.text: A sale (50% off) in large store almost finished? Very nice

indicators.note: in means the short pieces sit inside the trimmed store
almost finished means the word is stopped just before its end

parts.note: plenty is an ample supply, a large store

indicators.note: half off means only the first half of the word sale is kept

explanation.surface: A half-price sale is held in a big shop that is nearly sold out, which is lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% off' keeps SA, half of 'sale'; 'almost finished' drops the last letter of PLENTY. 'store' looks like a shop but means a supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Something agreeable or delightful is described as lovely or very nice.

clue.text: Industrial action once more: lawyers brought in to reach an agreement

parts.note: a strike is industrial action

indicators.note: brought in means the lawyers are placed inside the other word

parts.note: again means once more
the bar is the body of barristers, lawyers

explanation.surface: Workers walk out again until lawyers are brought in to settle the dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Industrial action' and 'lawyers' fit the surface of a labour dispute settled by negotiation, which is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To conclude a deal is to settle terms, an idiom for making a pact.

clue.text: Ancient Ur to be rebuilt? Doubtful

indicators.note: rebuilt suggests the letters of the old city phrase are put together anew

explanation.surface: Will the old Mesopotamian city of Ur ever be reconstructed?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be rebuilt' rearranges the nine letters of ANCIENT UR.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter that is unsure or open to question is dubious.

clue.text: OAP about to leave Scottish island

indicators.note: to leave means those letters are taken away

parts.note: an old-age pensioner is a retiree
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A pensioner is about to depart for a Hebridean isle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' removes RE (about) from RETIREE. 'about to leave' reads as 'soon to go'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiree is one of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.

clue.text: Tory accepting defeat? One might be in the soup

definitions.text: One might be in the soup

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the party letters surround the defeat

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, a Tory
a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician concedes defeat and finds themselves in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the soup' means in trouble, which suits the defeated Tory, but here it is literal: the garnish floats in soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A fried bread cube is a garnish floated in broth.

clue.text: Walls easily repaired by builder at the front

indicators.note: at the front picks out the opening letter of builder
repaired suggests the letters of easily are fixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A builder easily fixes some walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the front' places B first and takes it from 'builder'; 'repaired' rearranges EASILY to AILEYS. A bailey is a castle's outer wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer defensive ramparts of a castle are its curtain walls.

clue.text: Tissue to take care of blocked nose, suffering with a cold

parts.note: a chill is a cold

indicators.note: blocked means the care word sits inside, blocking the nose letters
suffering suggests the nose is in a bad way, so its letters are disordered

parts.note: to tend is to take care of

explanation.surface: A tissue is wanted to deal with a stuffy nose from a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges NOSE into ESON. 'Tissue' looks like a paper hanky for the cold but is body tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: The cord at the back of the heel is a band of fibrous tissue.

clue.text: Potty group conscious of a facial feature

parts.note: the chin is a feature of the face
aware means conscious

explanation.surface: A crazy band knows what its noses and chins look like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' reads as crazy, but a potty is a chamber pot, one item of porcelain crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelain crockery covers pots of all kinds, a chamber pot included.

clue.text: Stirring, dad began getting dressed

indicators.note: stirring means mixing, so the letters of dad began are mixed up

explanation.surface: Dad finally stirred and started putting his clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirring' rearranges DAD BEGAN; 'dressed' means a wound has been covered, not clothed.
explanation.definitionFit: A wound that is dressed has had a bandage or lint applied.

clue.text: Play a new version of Daniel by hot American group

indicators.note: a new version reworks the letters of Daniel into another order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a band is a group

explanation.surface: A fresh take on Daniel is performed by a sizzling US band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new version of' signals the anagram; 'by' is only a link. The play is a comedy by Oscar Wilde, so 'Play' is the definition, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a comedy by Oscar Wilde, a stage drama.

clue.text: Tragic Greek's name revealed in newspaper article

indicators.note: revealed in means the name letter appears inside the article word

parts.note: a leader is an editorial, a newspaper article

explanation.surface: A doomed Greek's identity is exposed in a press report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealed in' puts N inside LEADER. In myth, Leander drowned swimming the Hellespont to reach Hero.
explanation.definitionFit: This young man of Greek myth drowned crossing the Hellespont to his lover Hero.

clue.text: Policy changes party leader's introduced leading to periods of economic success

indicators.note: introduced means that letter is brought inside

parts.note: U-turns are reversals of policy

indicators.note: the leader of party is its first letter

explanation.surface: A party leader's policy reversals are credited with a booming economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader's' gives P from 'party'; 'introduced' puts it inside UTURNS. 'leading to' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Rises in trade or the market are improvements, times of growth.

clue.text: Eccentric sergeant, say, stationed in Cyprus

indicators.note: stationed in means the rank is posted inside the country code

parts.note: CY is the international code for Cyprus
sergeant is an example of a military rank

explanation.surface: An odd army sergeant is posted to Cyprus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sergeant, say' signals an example: the sergeant is one rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone odd or bad-tempered is described as crotchety or weird.

clue.text: Count showing a lord round estate, say, proceeding in wrong direction

indicators.note: going the wrong way means the whole run is read backwards
round means the lord's letters surround the car

parts.note: lud is a form of lord, as in m'lud
an estate is a type of car

explanation.surface: A nobleman shows a peer around his country estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' makes LUCARD and 'proceeding in wrong direction' turns A LUCARD backwards. An estate is a British station wagon; 'showing' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker's vampire held the noble title of count.

clue.text: Extremely tough sportsman, participant in discus event?

indicators.note: extremely points to the outermost letters of tough

parts.note: a rower is an oarsman, a sportsman

explanation.surface: A very hardy athlete competes in the discus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'tough', TH. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A discus competitor is one who hurls, an athlete who throws.

clue.text: Supplied with drink at home during the day

indicators.note: during means the home word falls inside the day

parts.note: Wed is short for Wednesday, a day
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone is given a drink at home in the daytime.
explanation.walkthrough: Wed is the usual short form of Wednesday.
explanation.definitionFit: To be served alcohol, as in dined and treated, is to be given drink.

clue.text: Quality of good people?

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: What is the virtue of virtuous folk?
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' joins the definition to the wordplay; the question mark hints that good people may have elegance or divine favour.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegance or charm of manner is an attractive attribute.

clue.text: Weapon with silver point taken by a knight, French hero …

parts.note: a dart is a thrown weapon
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
N is north, a compass point
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A swordsman carries a silver-tipped weapon in the service of a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next, but the two are solved apart. The hero is the Musketeer of Dumas.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumas's swashbuckling Gascon musketeer is a celebrated fictional Frenchman.

clue.text: … Barrymore depicted

definitions.meaning: the actress first-named for the American Barrymore acting family member
depicted means sketched or portrayed in a picture

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on from the previous clue for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: The actress of E.T. has this forename, and sketched is a synonym of depicted.

clue.text: Now feel peeved about dollar cut in salary

indicators.note: cut in means inserted, so the pieces go inside the salary word

parts.note: pay is salary
to resent is to feel peeved
D is an abbreviation for dollar

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed about a dollar cut from their wages right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' only joins, in the sense 'concerning'. 'Now' is adjectival, as in 'the now generation'.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the current time or contemporary, as in modern-day.
